```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is a paying customer within 90 days, so the payer section decides this. A cites a sourced, priced comparable in its adjacent category: CoFoundersLab at $29/mo or $299/yr, the only competitor with confirmed paid conversion. B says outright that 'no one is currently shown paying' for Free Pascal/Lazarus docs, and its most plausible institutional payer, the Foundation, funds development, not docs.",
    "B's own case against says its market is too small to sustain a one-person company. It also cites a 2012 thread suggesting the real blocker is maintainer unwillingness, which an outside docs site cannot fix. That undercuts both the payer and the product's effect.",
    "B's demand evidence is stronger and spans 2010–2024, but it shows frustration, not willingness to pay. A's demand is thinner (one Reddit post via a mirror) but comes from people trying to get apps built, which sits closer to a transaction.",
    "A's acquisition channel has a per-paying-customer cost estimate ($100–200 via niche community outreach), though it comes from a vendor blog. B's only quantified paid channel is a generic 2016 CPC benchmark the brief itself says is likely not Pascal-specific."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's payer hypothesis: a ~$50/month business tier for 'companies shipping commercial Lazarus-based products.' The only anchor is Read the Docs' general pricing. The brief names no such company and shows none expressing interest or paying for docs, so the one route to revenue is unevidenced.",
  "confidence_note": "Low confidence. Both briefs are weak on the 90-day paying-customer question. A has serious problems: the concept is unresolved ('one-line description to confirm'), the customer is listed as 'varies by idea', the niche is crowded with no-traction clones, and its only demand thread contains a direct community rebuttal ('you can just vibe code'). A wins narrowly because it shows at least an adjacent, sourced willingness to pay. B shows real pain but explicitly no payer."
}
```
